name: Wimberley Market Days
desc: First-Saturday open-air market running March through December. Booth spaces are assigned by seniority, with a rolling waitlist for new vendors. Approval is rolling via email (leasing@wimberleymarketday.com), not a fixed application deadline; booths are typically rented the week before each market day. Pricing is tiered: $125 is the standard monthly rate, with a discounted $75 summer-season rate (roughly Jun-Aug) and a separate $100 Friday-evening rate — this listing's Sept 5 date falls outside the summer window, so $125 is the applicable figure.

name: Fredericksburg Trade Days
desc: Three-day Hill Country market held the third weekend of each month across covered barns and open field lots. Pricing varies by space: $75-$135 for outdoor lots, $150-$273 for indoor barn spaces (10x14 to 15x14). No published application deadline or jury process; contact 210-846-4094 to book.

name: Bayou City Art Festival
desc: Juried fine art festival drawing a national applicant pool across 19 media categories. Panel review with blind scoring. This is the Memorial Park edition (Fri-Sun); booth fees range $525-$1775 by category/size plus a separate $50 non-refundable jury fee. Accepted artists notified by Jul 6. Public admission is $18 early-bird/$20 regular per day (kids 6-12 $5, 5 and under free), or $30 for a weekend pass.

name: Comicpalooza
desc: Multi-genre pop culture convention with a dedicated Artist Alley. Tables sell out in tiers; early registration opens to prior-year vendors. UNVERIFIED: 2027 exhibitor applications aren't open yet (interest form only as of Aug 2026) — no official 2027 dates, pricing, or deadline published. Current start/end/deadline/fee below are unconfirmed placeholders. Public admission ($68 single-day, ~$119 weekend pass) is reference pricing carried over from the completed May 2026 event via secondary media coverage — the official site no longer publishes 2026 prices and hasn't posted 2027 numbers yet.

name: Armadillo Christmas Bazaar
desc: Ten-day juried holiday art market with live music. Long-run format favors vendors with deep inventory and staffing help. Booth fees run ~$1,500-$5,000+ by size (avg ~$2,000) plus a $25 application fee. Applications are accepted year-round on a rolling basis; Jan-Mar submissions get priority, with primary review Mar-Aug. Returning artists get priority over new applicants in popular categories. Public admission is $12 (+fees, ~$14 total) per day, or $60 for a season pass; kids 12 and under free.

name: First Monday Trade Days
desc: One of the largest recurring open-air markets in the country, spanning several hundred acres over four days each month. UNVERIFIED: the grounds are split across many independently-operated pavilions, each with its own booth pricing and contact — there is no single official fee. Call the City of Canton First Monday office at 903-567-6556 for a specific venue's rate.

name: Cottonwood Art Festival
desc: Twice-yearly juried fine art festival in a shaded park setting. Jury reviews three work images plus one booth shot. $500 covers a single booth; a double booth is $1,000 (limited) and electricity is a $100 add-on. A separate $35 non-refundable jury/application fee is paid per entry via ZAPPlication.

name: Blue Genie Art Bazaar
desc: Consignment-model holiday bazaar. No booth fee or staffing requirement; the venue takes a percentage of sales instead, plus a $45 non-refundable application fee. The Yelp "Temporarily Closed" status is normal seasonal downtime, not a shutdown — the storefront is a holiday-only operation that reopens each November for the season, running Nov 13-Dec 24, 2026 (corrected from an earlier Nov 27 start). Public admission is believed free (multiple secondary sources agree; the official FAQ page returned a 404 during verification, so treat as likely rather than confirmed). The 2026 submission window ran May 1-Jul 31 and has already closed as of this listing's last check — this is now a "watch for next May's window" reference for vendors, not a currently-open call; the shop itself is still on for its Nov-Dec 2026 run.

name: Anime Matsuri
desc: Anime and Japanese culture convention with a large artist alley and separate dealer hall. Table assignment by registration order. Corrected from a stale March placeholder — Anime Matsuri actually runs in July; the 2026 edition (Jul 23-26) is confirmed and uncancelled, and 2027 is set for Jul 22-25 (per Eventbrite, though organizers note dates may shift). Applications open Sept 8 with price tiers increasing Dec 1/Mar 1/Apr 1/Jun 1 - exact table price not published outside the application form, so the $380 figure and Dec 1 "deadline" (first price-increase date) are best-effort estimates. Public admission tiers are $65 Fri/$70 Sat/$45 Sun from the official badge page, but tied to the just-completed 2026 dates and carried as reference pricing since 2027 isn't priced yet.

name: Main Street Fort Worth Arts Festival
desc: Four-day juried street festival with very high foot traffic. Booths are on pavement; weights required in place of stakes. Standard 10x10 booth is $995 (corner $1,145), plus a separate $40 non-refundable application fee. 220 artists are jury-selected from nearly 1,000 applicants (2026 cycle figure).

name: Emerald City Comic Con
desc: Artist Alley is curated via portfolio review, not a lottery or first-come order. Accepted artists get a 6' table plus 2 badges for $430. Corrected: 2027 applications are open, not closed — the real deadline is Oct 29, 2026 at 5:00pm PT, with notifications going out Nov 13, 2026 (an earlier version of this listing incorrectly showed a Jan 16, 2027 deadline and claimed applications had already closed with only a waitlist available). Public admission is $84 Saturday single-day (tax/fees included), $64.05 Fri/Sun, $27.30 Thursday preview — confirmed on the official 2027 ticket page.

name: Round Top Antiques Fair
desc: Roughly two-and-a-half-week destination market spread across 48+ independent show fields (not nine days as previously listed). Early fields like Bar W Field, Henkel Square, and The Marketplace Warrenton open Oct 15; most of the 48+ venues run the official Oct 17-31 window. Space is leased directly from individual field operators (e.g. Zapp Hall, Excess Fields, Marburger Farm, Big Red Barn) - pricing and application process vary by field and remain unconfirmed here; the $900 fee is an unverified placeholder. Public admission is similarly fragmented across the 48+ fields — most are free to browse, but the flagship "Original Round Top Antiques Fair" field charges its own $10 general/$25 VIP admission, so no single admission price applies to the market as a whole.

name: Texas Renaissance Festival
desc: Eight-weekend seasonal festival requiring period-appropriate merchandise and shop presentation. Multi-season vendors get renewal priority. Corrected start date: the official site confirms the 2026 season runs Oct 10-Nov 29 plus Thanksgiving Friday (the previously listed Oct 3 start was wrong — Oct 3 isn't part of the season). Confirmed: the vendor application itself carries a $50 non-refundable fee. The $1,400 figure here is presumed to be the actual shop/booth lease, but I could not confirm that number from the source PDF (binary-encoded, didn't extract cleanly) — needs a second look. No official application deadline is published — the site currently states it's still accepting new-vendor applications on a rolling basis, so the date shown is an estimated planning buffer, not a hard cutoff. Public admission is NOT free and has no single flat price — the official site confirms dynamic per-weekend pricing from roughly $16-27 (early/off-peak weekends like Oktoberfest) up to $28-46+ (peak weekends like Pirate Adventure, Halloween, Highland Fling), advance vs. gate. The $28 stored here is a typical non-peak gate-day figure, not an official constant.

name: Austin Flea
desc: Recurring indie maker pop-up hosted at rotating bars and venues. Low entry cost makes it a common first market for new vendors. Booths run $50-$75/event (varies by venue, listed per application) plus a $5/yr new-vendor tent/display approval fee. Each application is individually juried; Texas Sales Tax Permit required. Local, handmade/vintage sellers only — no imported goods.

name: Dallas Fan Expo
desc: Large pop culture convention with tiered artist alley pricing by table location and corner access. Corrected from a placeholder May 2027 date - the confirmed, upcoming edition is Sep 11-13, 2026 at the Kay Bailey Hutchison Convention Center (2027 dates aren't announced yet). Standard 6x5 table is $480; premium 5x12 end-cap is $1,060. No fixed application deadline is published - tables sell until they run out, so this date is an estimated planning buffer, not an official cutoff. Public single-day admission is $58 Saturday/$48 Sunday/$33 Friday per the official ticketing partner's live checkout page (base price before service fee) — confirmed as current pricing, though the site notes "advanced pricing" ends Aug 27, 2026 and may step up to a higher tier before the show.

name: Nutcracker Market
desc: Massive juried holiday shopping market fundraising for Houston Ballet, drawing over 100,000 shoppers across a preview party plus four show days at NRG Center. Unlike a flat booth-fee model, Houston Ballet also takes an 11% commission on merchant sales on top of space cost, and charges a separate non-refundable $25 application fee. Exact booth pricing tiers weren't accessible (pricing page blocked automated access), so the $2,500 fee here is a rough placeholder based on comparable high-traffic juried holiday markets, not a confirmed price - confirm real pricing and the application deadline directly before applying. Public admission is $20/day general, or $60 for a 4-day early-bird pass; kids 2 and under free.

name: Denton Arts & Jazz Festival
desc: Long-running juried art show paired with a large free jazz festival, recently relocated to the North Texas Fairgrounds and shifted from its traditional spring slot to Sep 11-13, 2026 (worth double-checking before relying on the old April date elsewhere). 10x10 booths available indoor/outdoor; a $50/exhibitor surcharge applies for shared booths. Jun 1 is the no-surcharge cutoff, not a hard close - late fees of $20 (after Jun 1) and $50 (after Aug 1) suggest applications are still accepted this close to the show, just at a premium; the Aug 20 date here is an estimated last-call, not an official cutoff. Base booth fee was never published anywhere I could find - the $300 here is an unverified estimate, not a confirmed price. Attendance (~200k) is the festival's historical figure from its old Quakertown Park venue and may not hold at the new fairgrounds site.

name: Boerne Market Days
desc: Recurring Hill Country market on Boerne's historic Main Plaza, held the second weekend of every month, plus three bonus special-event dates not reflected in this listing's auto-computed schedule: a November Holiday Gift Market and two separate December markets (a Christmas Market and a Cowboy Christmas Market) — the organizer's own site cites these three extra dates in its attendance figures. Vendors reapply each month they want to participate. Booth fees must be paid by the 1st of the month before the show and are non-refundable, but the actual dollar amount isn't published online - the $40 here is a rough estimate based on comparable small-town Hill Country markets, not a confirmed price. Contact davidquerbach@eventsoffmain.com or (210) 844-8193 to confirm current pricing and attendance before applying. Public admission is inferred free — the official page lists public market hours with no fee mentioned, but there's no explicit "free" statement either.

name: Pancakes & Booze Art Show
desc: Traveling one-night "anti-gallery" art show at The Far Out Lounge & Stage — free pancakes, full bar, live body-painting, 75+ local artists showing 300+ pieces. 18+ event. No jury and no commission: accepted artists just pay a flat per-piece wall-hanging fee (the $15 here is a national average figure, not Austin-confirmed — the org states it varies by city). A separate vendor lane exists for craft/product sellers, but no table fee is published. Applications are rolling until the venue fills, so the deadline shown is an estimated planning buffer, not an official cutoff. Public admission is $17 early-bird / $23 day-of (confirmed via Eventbrite). Attendance is a rough estimate based on comparable Pancakes & Booze editions in other cities — no official total is published.

name: Art & Beer Night Market Austin
desc: Annual evening market at The Brewtorium pairing 70+ local artists/makers with craft beer and food. Confirmed to have run in both 2024 (Nov 9) and 2025 (Nov 8) — both landed on the 2nd Saturday of November, which is the pattern this listing's date is computed from, but the 2026 edition hasn't been officially announced yet, so treat the date as inferred, not confirmed. Booth fee, public admission price, and application deadline are all unconfirmed — no organizer page publishes dollar figures; the $75 fee shown is a rough estimate based on comparable small Austin maker markets. Outdoor/brewery-grounds setting is inferred from the venue, not explicitly stated. Watch the organizer's Instagram (@artandbeeraustin) for the official 2026 announcement before applying.

name: Fiesta Arts Fair
org: UT San Antonio (Southwest School of Art)
desc: Nationally-ranked juried fine art & craft fair (Top 50, Art Fair SourceBook) held on UTSA's historic Southwest campus as part of Fiesta San Antonio, drawing 100-120+ artists from ~30 states. The Nov 1, 2026 application deadline is real and actionable — applications for the next edition just opened via ZAPPlication — but the show's own 2027 dates aren't announced yet; the Apr 17-18, 2027 shown here is an estimated placeholder following the fair's usual mid-to-late-April slot. Booth fee ($350+) is a stale figure from a 2017-18 secondary source, not confirmed current pricing. The separate ZAPPlication jury/application fee is confirmed current: $25 early-bird (until 9/8/2026), $30 standard, $35 late (after 11/2/2026). Public admission ($16 for a 2-day ticket) is confirmed for the just-completed April 2026 edition. Attendance is a rough midpoint of conflicting secondary estimates (8,000-12,000).

name: Old Gruene Market Days
desc: Long-running monthly artisan market (~100 vendors) in the Gruene Historic District selling handmade crafts and Texas-made packaged foods, with free live entertainment. Runs the 3rd full weekend of the month, February through November, plus a bonus 1st-weekend-of-December date not reflected in this listing's auto-computed schedule (same modeling limitation as Boerne's extra December date — see README). It is juried, so it's not a walk-on market, but no application deadline is published anywhere the organizer's site would confirm (site blocked automated access) — shown as rolling until confirmed; contact the Gruene Merchants Association directly. Booth fee ($60) is an estimate based on comparable small monthly Hill Country markets, not an organizer-published figure. Admission and parking are confirmed free. Attendance (~4,000/weekend) is a secondary-source estimate, not an official organizer figure.

name: Hub City Art & Craft Vendor Market
desc: Small, three-day indie craft/art market for local artists, crafters, and small boutique businesses (jewelry, candles, fine art, woodworking, home decor, specialty foods with approval) at the Municipal Garden & Arts Center. Application is informal — a direct email to the organizer (jeremysanders612@gmail.com) rather than a jury or formal platform — making it a genuinely low-barrier option for new/emerging vendors, though that also means little published pricing data. Booth fee, public admission, and attendance are all unconfirmed estimates based on comparable small local markets; confirm directly with the organizer before applying.

name: Chalk the Block
org: City of El Paso Museums and Cultural Affairs Department
desc: Large, free, city-run public arts festival in Downtown El Paso combining a major chalk-art competition (judged, with a $2,000 "Best of Show" prize) with an artisan/cottage-food vendor market and food trucks — one of the best-attended events in this directory, with attendance confirmed across multiple independent sources. Note: the 2026 artisan-vendor application deadline (Jul 31) has already passed as of this listing's verification date — treat this as a "watch for next year's application window, expect similar October timing" reference rather than a currently-open call. Vendor booth fee is unconfirmed (no dollar figure published); the $150 shown is a rough estimate based on comparable city-run festival vendor fees. Public admission is confirmed free.

name: Dia de los Muertos Arts & Crafts Expo
desc: Juried arts-and-crafts expo ("Hecho a Mano") embedded in Corpus Christi's large annual Dia de los Muertos street festival, now in its 19th year and repeatedly named a top Dia de los Muertos celebration nationally. Single booth (10'x10') is $125, double is $250 (roughly doubling to $250/$500 if paid late, after Oct 1), plus a separate non-refundable $10 application fee; a mandatory vendor meeting is held before the event. Public admission is confirmed free (a separate ticketed VIP preview party is optional/extra). Overall public attendance isn't published anywhere official — the $8,000 shown is a rough estimate based on the festival's scale (85-100+ vendor booths) and its repeated "best festival" recognition, not a confirmed figure.

name: Art in the Square
desc: Long-running (26+ years) juried fine art festival at Southlake Town Square, run entirely by volunteers of the Southlake Women's Club to benefit Tarrant County charities, drawing 150+ artists and repeatedly ranked #1 by Art Fair SourceBook. Single booth (10'x10') is $550, double is $1,050, and there's a distinctive $300 Emerging Artist tier for developing DFW-area artists — plus a separate $40 non-refundable application fee. Public admission is confirmed free. Attendance is reported as "tens of thousands" across organizer and third-party sources, but no precise official total is published — the 40,000 shown is an order-of-magnitude estimate, not a hard count.

name: Celebration of the Arts
desc: Self-described cornerstone fine art & fine craft event of the Permian Basin, now in its 42nd+ year, held fully indoors (rain-or-shine, air-conditioned) at the Bush Convention Center with 40+ regional/out-of-state artists across painting, fiber, photography, jewelry, wood, and glass, plus cash jury awards. The just-completed 43rd edition's booth fee was never published beyond a $25 non-refundable ZAPPlication application fee — the $450 shown is a rough estimate based on comparably-sized indoor Texas art fairs, not an organizer-confirmed price. 2027 show dates aren't announced yet (next cycle typically opens in December); the May 14-16 window shown is an estimated placeholder following the fair's usual mid-May slot. Saturday/Sunday admission is confirmed free (a separate ticketed Friday preview party is $80-85, not general admission). Attendance is unconfirmed — no official total is published; 5,000 is a conservative estimate for a regional indoor fair of this size.

name: Rose Festival Arts and Crafts Fair
desc: Long-running fair paired with the historic Texas Rose Festival at Bergfeld Park, with 90-100+ booths of handcrafted goods (jewelry, candles, pottery, wreaths, mixed-media art) plus live music and food trucks. Data quality here is thinner than most listings: the City of Tyler's own event pages are currently unreachable (404/site restructure), so the booth fee was never independently confirmed — the $55 shown is an estimate based on comparable small regional craft fairs, not an official figure. Jury status is reported by a secondary source (FestivalNet) but not independently verified on an official page. Confirm current pricing directly with City of Tyler Parks & Rec (~903-531-1214) before applying. Admission is confirmed free; attendance (~3,000) is also a secondary-source estimate, not an official City of Tyler figure.

name: Beaumont Comic Con
desc: Small, multi-year-running regional pop-culture convention at Doggett Ford Park in Beaumont, with costume contests, cosplay meetups, and vendor/artist booths. Vendor space is a flat $100 for a 10x10 (includes 1 table, 2 chairs, 2 vendor badges), confirmed on the official site. No formal application portal or deadline is published — inquiries go through beaumontcon@yahoo.com, so the date shown here is an estimated planning buffer, not an official cutoff. Public admission and attendance are unconfirmed for the 2026 edition specifically (a news article cites $12/$10 tickets, but for dates that don't match this year's Oct 3-4 show, so it may reflect a stale prior year) — fills the otherwise-empty Golden Triangle (Beaumont/Port Arthur/Orange) region.

name: Galveston Craft Show
desc: Juried, handmade-only indoor craft show relocating for 2027 to the Moody Gardens Hotel and Convention Center ("The Founding Year at Moody Gardens"), still run alongside the Corvette/Chevy Expo on one shared ticket. Pricing changed with the venue move: a standard 10x10 booth is now $125 (corner booths, limited availability, are $155) — no longer bundled with admission passes as in prior years at the old Convention Center venue. Vendor applications open Aug 1, 2026 and are juried (curated for product quality/category balance); no fixed application deadline is published, so the date shown here is an estimated planning buffer, not an official cutoff. Public admission is $18 one-day advance / $20 at door, $30-35 for a weekend pass; free for kids 12 and under. Attendance is an estimate carried from the prior venue — unconfirmed for the new location.

name: ArtWalk Alpine
desc: Billed as the longest-running art festival in West Texas, now in its 33rd year — murals, sculpture, photography, and painting fill downtown Alpine's sidewalks and studios over the weekend, alongside two music stages and food trucks. Free to attend and explicitly non-juried, with ~26 exhibitors historically. Booth fee is genuinely not published anywhere online (only a downloadable PDF application is offered) — the $65 shown is a rough estimate based on comparable small non-juried outdoor art walks, not an organizer-confirmed price; request the application directly to learn the real cost. Nov 20-21 dates are confirmed directly on the official site (a secondary source's Nov 20-22 listing does not match and appears to be wrong). Fills the far West Texas / Big Bend region gap.

name: Lunada Artisan Market
desc: Recurring evening outdoor artisan market at Southern Pacific Linear Park (6-10pm), run directly by Brownsville Parks & Recreation — fills the Rio Grande Valley gap. Not a clean monthly cadence: only a handful of dates run per year (Jan/Mar/May/Sep in 2026, per the city's current published calendar), registered first-come-first-served for $40/event via the city's RecDesk portal — no jury, no application deadline. The date and deadline shown here reflect the next confirmed 2026 date (Sep 19); check the city page for the year's full schedule since it isn't a fixed recurring rule this site can auto-compute. Admission is confirmed free; attendance is unconfirmed — the 800 shown is a rough estimate for a single city-park evening market, not an official figure.

name: Abilene Holiday Market
desc: Juried, single-day indoor holiday gift market at the Mesquite Event Center in downtown Abilene, with 50+ vendors selling handmade and unique goods — fills the Big Country/West-Central Texas region gap. Tiered booth pricing: 5x10 $75, 10x10 $150, 10x15 $200, 10x20 $300, edible vendors (5x8) $50, plus a $10 non-refundable application fee (photos required); organizers explicitly select for handmade/unique quality and event fit. Public admission is $5 general, $3 with student/teacher/military ID, free for kids 11 and under. All core figures — fee tiers, admission, ~1,800 average attendance — are confirmed directly from the organizer's page.

name: San Japan
desc: Large annual anime/gaming convention at the Henry B. Gonzalez Convention Center, held Labor Day weekend. Confirmed 2025 attendance was 32,073 badge-holders (75,000+ turnstile count across 3 days). Artist Alley uses a lottery, not a jury: signup opened Apr 27, 2026 and closed May 10, 2026 (or at 1,250 applications), with acceptances issued by May 30 - this 2026 lottery window has already closed as of this listing's verification date; treat this as a reference for the next lottery, expected to open ~late April 2027. A fan-art table is $285 + 3% platform fee for a 6'x30" table, one badge, two chairs (max 3 extra badges at $90-100 each). ~275 tables available for ~1,250 applicants. Public admission: Saturday single-day is $52.10 online (3-day passes run $72.50-$95 depending on when purchased, on-site up to $13 higher) - figure shown is the Saturday walk-in rate. Vendor sentiment is largely positive (spacious alley, robust dealer room); the one recurring complaint found is unreliable convention-center wifi/cell signal causing occasional card-payment failures.

name: Mission Marquee Farmers & Artisans Market
desc: Recurring artisan/farmers market at Mission Marquee Plaza near San Antonio's Mission Reach (Mar-Nov). CONFIRMED: no vendor fee is charged ("No vendor fees will apply" per the official page) - genuinely rare for this directory. Application is via an online Smartsheet form with no fixed deadline; acceptance isn't guaranteed and the plaza reserves discretion over vendor mix, so treated as non-juried/discretionary rather than a formal panel jury. Artisan goods must be handmade - no mass-produced items. Runs BOTH the 1st and 3rd Saturday of each month; this listing's auto-computed schedule follows the 3rd Saturday only (same modeling limitation as Boerne/Gruene's bonus dates - see README), so a 1st-Saturday date each month isn't reflected here. Public admission and attendance are unconfirmed - inferred free (no fee mentioned for visitors) and estimated at a modest 1,500/market day for a single mission-plaza market, not an official figure.

name: Frisco Maker Faire
desc: Free, all-ages maker showcase at the Frisco Discovery Center / Sci-Tech Discovery Center, grant-funded so there is genuinely no fee for makers or attendees. The 2026 edition ran Jan 31, 2026 (regular registration closed Dec 15, 2025, late registration to Jan 5, 2026) - that date has already passed as of this listing's verification, so the Jan 30, 2027 date and Dec 15, 2026 deadline shown here are estimated based on the prior year's pattern, not yet officially announced. Open to any "maker" - digital, physical, arts, or music - with December applicants getting priority placement (not a formal jury). Indoor, with overflow to the adjacent Sci-Tech museum galleries. Attendance is unconfirmed - no official figure published; 3,000 is a rough estimate for a single-day free family STEM/maker event of this scale.

name: Frisco Holiday Gift Market
desc: Single-evening city-run holiday market at Simpson Plaza (3-7:30pm) paired with Santa photos, carriage rides, and a tree-lighting ceremony. CONFIRMED: applications close Nov 1, 2026 (or earlier if booths fill), reviewed in order received starting Sep 1; the vendor committee has discretion over quality/fit rather than running a formal blind jury. Each booth includes a 10'x10' tent with lighting, one 6' table, two chairs, a 4-outlet power box, and two parking passes - an unusually full amenity bundle for the fee. UNVERIFIED: exact booth dollar cost isn't published on the official page - the $100 shown is an estimate based on comparably-bundled city-run holiday markets, not a confirmed price; confirm directly via friscotexas.gov before applying. Admission is inferred free (standard for this kind of civic plaza holiday event; not explicitly stated). Attendance is unconfirmed - 5,000 is a rough single-evening estimate.

name: Plano International Festival
desc: One-day multicultural festival at Haggard Park, Downtown Plano, confirmed for Oct 17, 2026, 11am-5pm, with free admission and parking. Cultural/community vendor booths display and sell cultural artifacts, artwork, textiles, jewelry, and similar goods (religious/political material explicitly prohibited). CONFIRMED tiered booth fees: $300 commercial, $150 small business (3 employees or fewer), $100 non-profit/cultural/civic, +$50 per extra table+2 chairs - the $150 small-business tier is shown as representative; actual cost depends on vendor category. Application deadline confirmed as Aug 31, 2026. Not a formal jury - vendor category and content rules apply instead. Attendance is unconfirmed - no official figure published; 15,000 is a rough estimate for a free single-day downtown multicultural festival of this type.

name: Round Rock Market Days
desc: Recurring monthly artisan/vendor fair at Prete Main Street Plaza in Downtown Round Rock, first Saturday of the month March-December (October shifts to the 2nd Saturday - not reflected in this listing's auto-computed schedule, same modeling limitation as Boerne/Gruene's bonus dates). ~120 exhibitors, free admission and parking, live music. CONFIRMED booth fee tiers are $85/$100 depending on space (exact tier criteria not published) - $85 shown as the representative figure. Spaces are first-come-first-served rather than formally juried. No fixed application deadline is published; the date shown is an estimated planning buffer. Attendance is unconfirmed - 6,000 is a rough estimate for a well-attended monthly downtown market of this size, not an official figure.

name: Red Poppy Festival
desc: Georgetown's flagship annual festival (27th edition in 2026), three days on the historic downtown square with live music and 100-150+ artisan vendors selling handmade-only work. CONFIRMED: 2027 dates are officially set (Apr 23-25). Booth fees confirmed for the most recent cycle: $400 for a 10'x10', $800 for a 10'x20', plus a separate $25 non-refundable application fee. Selection is via photo/portfolio review with a handmade-only certification requirement (not a blind panel jury, but not open walk-on either). The Jan 8, 2027 deadline shown is an estimate extrapolated from the prior cycle's Jan 9, 2026 deadline - the 2027 application window wasn't open yet as of this listing's verification. Admission is confirmed free. Attendance (~75,000 over the weekend) is confirmed via the city's special events coordinator.

name: Spring Market in the Vines
desc: Small single-day vendor market held outdoors at 3 Texans Winery and Vineyard, paired with wine tasting and live music. CONFIRMED (from the official vendor rules page): $70 per 10'x10' booth, application and payment due by 5pm the Thursday before the market day, no refunds, and organizers reserve discretion to limit duplicate product categories among vendors (curated rather than open walk-on). Only one market day per year has been publicly scheduled in recent cycles - the 2026 edition ran May 9, 2026, which has already passed as of this listing's verification, so the May 8, 2027 date and May 6, 2027 deadline shown here are estimated based on the prior year's pattern, not yet officially announced. General market/browsing admission is inferred free (winery tasting fees are separate and not an entry charge, but this isn't explicitly confirmed) - left as null pending confirmation. Attendance is unconfirmed - 500 is a rough estimate for a small single-venue winery market.

name: McAllen Farmers Market
desc: Recurring weekly artisan/farmers market at the McAllen Public Library grounds (also marketed as "The Market @ McAllen"), running every Saturday 10am-1pm year-round except Thanksgiving and major holidays. CONFIRMED: juried entry - new artisan vendors submit photos of their work with the application and may be subject to studio inspection before approval. CONFIRMED tiered vendor fees: $40/month standard (first-come booth assignment), a discounted $30/month premium tier for vendors who prepay 4 months in advance (with an assigned space), or $5-$10/Saturday for farmers depending on value-added product mix - the $40 shown is the representative standard monthly rate, not a single-day drop-in fee. Vendors commit to a minimum 40 of 50 weeks/year (max 10 absences). No fixed application deadline - reviewed on a rolling basis before market days; date shown here is an estimated planning buffer. Public admission is confirmed free. Attendance is unconfirmed - 2,000 is a rough estimate for a well-established year-round regional farmers/artisan market, not an official figure. This is a genuinely weekly market (every Saturday), which doesn't fit this site's Nth-weekday recurrence engine, so it's listed as a plain static next-date entry rather than an auto-computed recurring one.

name: South Padre Island Market Days Show
desc: Long-running (25th annual as of the most recent cycle) indoor vendor show at the South Padre Island Convention Center, held twice per winter season: a 3-day January show and a separate 3-day February show (Fri/Sat 9am-5pm, Sun 10am-4pm) - this listing tracks the January date; the February show (confirmed Feb 19-21, 2027) isn't separately reflected here. Described by an independent local news source as "the largest indoor market in South Texas," drawing both local and out-of-state vendors. CONFIRMED: most vendor spaces are indoors, with outdoor spaces under covered structure. Entry is curated - prospective vendors email contact info plus photos of their merchandise for review, not an open first-come booth rental. UNVERIFIED: exact booth fee is not published anywhere online (organizers only take email inquiries) - the $150 shown is an estimate based on comparable multi-day indoor Texas vendor shows, not a confirmed price; email spimarketdays@gmail.com or call (956) 345-5022 to confirm. Public admission is confirmed at $2 (an older article cites $1, suggesting the price has since risen). Attendance is unconfirmed - 8,000 is a rough estimate for a show billed as the region's largest indoor market across a 3-day run.

name: Peddler's Jingle Mingle Marketplace
desc: Juried holiday-themed craft/gift marketplace at the Amarillo Civic Center Complex, part of the national touring Peddler Show brand. CONFIRMED via FestivalNet: 90 exhibitors, ~7,000 attendance, juried entry with a stated 'strict vetting process' for product/brand fit. Official policy is applications open 'until full' rather than a fixed cutoff - the Sep 9, 2026 date shown is an estimated planning buffer, not an official deadline. UNVERIFIED: exact booth fee - the official 2026 vendor contract PDF didn't extract cleanly (binary-encoded), so the $275 shown is an estimate based on comparable multi-day juried regional holiday craft shows, not a confirmed price; contact info@peddlershow.com to confirm. Public admission is $10-$25 depending on ticket type/day - $15 shown as a representative single-day figure. Sentiment is thin but not negative: a 3.7/5 rating from only 3 reviews on 10times.com, with one comment noting a past edition felt 'pretty small ... would have been better with more booths.'

name: Ark-La-Tex Tattoo & Art Expo
desc: Annual tattoo and art convention at the Maude Cobb Convention Center, now in its 7th+ year (documented running since at least 2022) with consistent positive local news coverage each cycle (KLTV) describing it as friendly and growing in both artists and attendees. CONFIRMED: ~140 artists at the 2025/2026 editions; admission $20 day pass / $40 weekend pass, free for kids 12 and under; features judged tattoo competitions (Best of Day $250, Best of Show $1,000) plus art exhibits and vendor booths. The 2026 edition ran May 15-17, 2026, already past as of this listing's verification - the May 14-16, 2027 date shown is estimated by extrapolating the event's consistent mid-May pattern, not yet officially announced. UNVERIFIED: exact artist/vendor booth fee is not published on the official site (registration links exist but no dollar figures) - the $350 shown is an estimate based on comparable regional tattoo/art conventions, not confirmed; overall attendance is similarly unconfirmed - 5,000 is a rough estimate for a 3-day regional expo of this scale, not an official figure. Note: a separate, newer one-off Texarkana edition of this same brand ran March 2026 with far less track record - this listing tracks the flagship, multi-year Longview edition only.

name: Longview Jaycees Trade Days
desc: Recurring general trade-days market (buy/sell/trade/swap) at the Longview Convention Complex Exhibit Center, held the second full weekend of every month EXCEPT September, when the venue instead hosts the annual Gregg County Fair. CONFIRMED tiered booth fees: $50/weekend for an inside 10x10 space, $45/weekend for an outside 10x20 space, plus $3/day for electricity. Not juried - vendors of all kinds are accepted first-come. No fixed application deadline is published (call 903-753-4478 for availability); the date shown is an estimated planning buffer. Admission and parking are confirmed free. Attendance is unconfirmed - 3,000 is a rough estimate for a monthly regional trade-days market of this size, not an official figure.

name: Cactus Market Days
desc: Recurring monthly local art and craft market held downtown San Angelo at 17 East Twohig, across from the historic Cactus Hotel, every third Saturday 10am-4pm. CONFIRMED (via Discover San Angelo and San Angelo LIVE!): free admission, handcrafted candles, jewelry, wood products, leather, and metal art, plus a food truck and local DJ. Application is informal - contact event coordinator Judy Fowler at 325-949-6200 directly - no formal jury or online portal found, so juried is shown as false and the deadline here is an estimated planning buffer, not an official cutoff. UNVERIFIED: booth fee is not published anywhere online - the $40 shown is an estimate based on comparable small monthly Texas downtown markets, not a confirmed price; attendance (1,500) is similarly a rough estimate, not an official figure.

name: Anime Frontier
desc: Annual anime convention at the Fort Worth Convention Center, launched 2021 (after COVID delays) and growing steadily since - Wikipedia documents 13,000 attendees in 2021, 16,000 in 2022, and Artist Alley expanding 50% by 2023. CONFIRMED: Artist Alley inline table is $365 (1 table, 2 chairs, 2 badges); selection is a curated application, not open registration - accepted artists are notified after review. The 2026 Artist Alley application window has already closed (closed Jun 5, 2026, notifications by Jun 26) as of this listing's verification - treat this as a reference for the 2027 cycle, expected to open similarly mid-year. UNVERIFIED: public admission price could not be confirmed (official ticket page blocked automated access) - left as null pending confirmation; check animefrontier.com/tickets directly. Attendance is an estimate extrapolating the documented growth trend past the last confirmed 2022 figure, not an official current count.

name: The Boho Market at Castle Hills Market
desc: Recurring stop of the Dallas-based, multi-city Boho Market touring pop-up at Castle Hills Market (2211 NW Military Hwy), a San Antonio-area shopping center; this brand also runs regular markets in Dallas, McKinney, and The Woodlands. CONFIRMED: curation explicitly excludes MLM/direct-sales, made-to-order food, and drop-shipped goods - locally made, handcrafted, or vintage only. Applications reviewed 3-7 business days after submission via the official vendor portal, with a published cancellation policy (50% refund 30+ days out, full forfeiture within 30 days) - a level of process transparency notably above most small local markets. Confirmed 2026 Castle Hills dates run roughly every 2 months (Apr 25, Jun 6, Sep 19, Dec 5); this listing tracks the Sep 19 date. UNVERIFIED: exact booth fee isn't published (vendors are invoiced after acceptance) - the $95 shown is an estimate based on comparable Texas touring pop-up markets, not a confirmed price. Admission is confirmed free. Attendance is unconfirmed - 2,000 is a rough estimate for a single stop of an established multi-city brand, not an official figure.

name: Home For the Holidays Gift Market
org: Home For The Holidays Gift Market
desc: Three-day indoor holiday gift market at the Waco Convention Center (Chisholm & McLennan Hall), part of a multi-city touring brand that also runs editions in Humble and other Texas cities. CONFIRMED: 130+ vendors selling handmade gifts, boutique clothing, home decor, and specialty foods; shopping hours run Friday 'First Call' 9am-noon through Sunday 4pm; kids 12 and under free. CONFIRMED admission: $10 First Call early-access ticket, $6 general admission (both re-admit with wristband). UNVERIFIED: vendor booth fee, application deadline, and total attendance are not published on the organizer's site - the $200 fee shown is an estimate based on comparable multi-day indoor holiday craft/gift shows (Peddler's Jingle Mingle, Frisco Holiday Gift Market), not a confirmed price; the Sep 15 deadline is an estimated planning buffer; attendance (5,000) is a rough estimate for a 3-day, 130-vendor indoor show, not an official figure. Fills a total gap - no prior listing in Waco.

name: Sugar Land Arts & Music Festival
desc: Juried fine-art festival relocating for 2026 to Sugar Land Town Square, a walkable open-air setting - a new flagship venue for the event. CONFIRMED (via CW39 news coverage): 100+ juried artists across 16 fine-art mediums, 6,000+ expected attendees, and admission free for the first time in the festival's history ('art should be accessible to everyone'). The 2026 application deadline (May 31, 2026) has already passed as of this listing's verification - treat as a reference for the 2027 cycle. UNVERIFIED: exact booth fee isn't published beyond the organizer's claim of 'one of the most competitive booth fees in Texas' - the $350 shown is an estimate based on comparable Texas fine-art fairs (Cottonwood, Denton), not a confirmed price. Fills a total gap - no prior listing in Sugar Land/Fort Bend County.

name: The Woodlands Fine Craft, Art & Design Show
desc: Indoor juried craft/design show at The Woodlands Waterway Marriott Hotel Town Center North Exhibit Hall, debuting under this new name in 2026 as a rebrand of the long-running Texas Fine Craft Show. CONFIRMED: 60 juried artists/designers across Jewelry & Wearable Design, Art & Sculpture, and Fine Craft & Home Decor; $35 ZAPPlication jury/application fee (up to 2 applications per artist); the 2026 application cycle is invitation-only/access-code gated per ZAPPlication, and the open window has already closed as of this listing's verification. CONFIRMED admission: $17 single-day / $22 weekend general (student/military/senior discounted), kids 12 and under free with a ticketed adult. UNVERIFIED: exact booth fee and total attendance are not published - the $450 fee shown is an estimate based on comparable indoor juried craft shows, not a confirmed price; attendance (5,000) is a rough estimate for a 60-artist, 2-day indoor hotel-convention-center show. Fills a total gap - no prior listing in The Woodlands.

name: Heart of Katy Fall Market
desc: Semi-annual (spring and fall) indoor craft show held inside Katy High School, run as a fundraiser by the Katy Bengal Brigade and Cheerleaders booster club. CONFIRMED: 100+ vendor booths selling handmade and some resale items, free admission and parking, non-juried entry, ~2,000 attendance. UNVERIFIED: booth fee is not published anywhere online - vendors must email heartofkatycraftshow@gmail.com or call 832-464-5476 for pricing; the $85 shown is an estimate based on comparable indoor school-gym craft shows, not a confirmed price. No fixed application deadline is published; the date shown is an estimated planning buffer.

name: Hangar Holiday Vendor Bazaar
desc: Long-running (started 1984 at Sheppard AFB) indoor holiday craft and vendor bazaar at the Wichita Falls MPEC, hosted by the Sheppard Spouses' Club with net proceeds funding scholarships and grants for military spouses and dependents. CONFIRMED: free admission, indoor venue, 220+ vendors - independently described as the largest free-admission craft/vendor show in the Greater Texoma area. UNVERIFIED: exact booth fee isn't published online (application is a Zeffy-hosted contract) - the $100 shown is an estimate based on comparable multi-day charity craft bazaars, not a confirmed price; attendance (7,000) and the application deadline are similarly rough estimates, not official figures.

name: FallsCon
desc: Family-friendly tabletop/TTRPG/board-gaming convention at the Wichita Falls MPEC, started 2016 and now a 501(c)3 nonprofit (since late 2022) supporting academic financial aid. CONFIRMED: $100 per 10x10 vendor booth (includes 8' table, 2 passes, power), juried application (approval not guaranteed, prioritized by variety/programming/space). Attendance has grown from 400+ (2023) to 600+ (2024); one source separately cites 452 tickets for the most recent cycle, a discrepancy likely reflecting different counting methods (unique tickets vs. total attendance) - 650 shown here is a conservative growth-trend estimate, not an official count. The 2027 edition has shifted to May (prior years ran April) - dates are confirmed via the official vendor page, though not yet independently cross-confirmed elsewhere. Admission ($15 Fri/Sun, $25 Sat, $40 weekend) is carried over from the most recently completed cycle as reference pricing, not yet confirmed for 2027.

name: San Marcos Fall Craft & Vendor Market
desc: Outdoor seasonal pop-up market at Tanger Outlets San Marcos, run by the multi-city touring brand Hometown Vendor Market (which also runs Valentine's and Spring editions in San Marcos). CONFIRMED: two-day booth $300, one-day booth $125 (all fees non-refundable), non-juried first-come-first-served entry with loose category caps for diversity. NOTE ON SENTIMENT: research turned up genuinely mixed vendor experiences with this brand - an A+ BBB rating and several strongly positive multi-year testimonials, alongside at least one report of disorganization/no-shows on the vendor list and a "scam alert" post from the brand's own page reiterating its no-refund policy. Not majority-negative, but worth vendors' own diligence before booking. Admission is inferred free (standard for an outlet-mall pop-up, not explicitly confirmed). Attendance is unconfirmed - 3,000 is a rough estimate, not an official figure.

name: Islander Lights Arts & Crafts Market
org: Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi Student Activities
desc: Single-evening arts & crafts market held indoors in the University Center Lonestar Ballroom, part of TAMU-CC's larger campus-wide Islander Lights holiday celebration (petting zoo, Santa photos, bounce houses, tree lighting). CONFIRMED: free admission, handmade-only vendor rule (no commercial/resale goods), attendant required at each table. UNVERIFIED: the source describing this as the "20th annual" event didn't clearly state which calendar year that milestone applies to, so the Nov 20, 2026 date shown is an estimate following the festival's usual mid-to-late-November pattern, not independently confirmed for 2026; the Nov 13 deadline is similarly extrapolated from a prior cycle's "apply by Nov 14" pattern. Booth fee isn't published online - the $50 shown is an estimate based on comparable small campus craft markets, not a confirmed price. Attendance is unconfirmed - 5,000 is a rough estimate for an established, well-attended annual campus community festival.
